rationale:
- `enabled_dependencies` (the only seed of dependency/`use`d crates into `plugins::active_plugins`): the dependency loop requires `!plugins.is_disabled(pms, id)` before `is_auto_enabled || is_used`; the `use` loop requires `!plugins.is_disabled(pms, &named)`. `is_disabled` uses `name_matches`, so `disable` beats `auto-enable = ["*"]` and any `use` entry, under cargo's hyphen/underscore rule.
- `decide` tests `is_disabled` first and returns `Declined`, so `discover`/`status` agree with activation.

Tests (all pass): `discovery::tests::use_entry_and_disable_outrank_the_standing_decisions` (`auto-enable = ["*"]` + `disable = ["widget-lib"]` -> declined, not auto-enabled); `discovery::tests::enabled_dependencies_reads_config_not_offers` (`clap` in `disable` is absent from the enabled list); `tests/enablement.rs` `plugins_entries_match_crate_names_like_cargo` (`auto-enable = ["*"]` + `disable = ["crate_a"]` -> `sync` installs nothing).

Scope limit (as the chapter note says): `disable` is not checked in `active_plugins`/`record_active`, so it blocks neither registry plugins nor a crate reached through a `[[plugins]]` chain edge. That also covers a chain from a *consented dependency* crate to a disabled dependency, which the note does not mention explicitly; the `decide` comment "Activation agrees (see `record_active`)" overstates this. I judged the requirement as written for dependency enablement and `use` (what it names) and flag the chain case for maintainer review.

**Refuted on review:** The requirement is violated when a disabled dependency plugin is reached through a `[[plugins]]` chain from a consented dependency. In that case `auto-enable` names the crate too, which is exactly the case the requirement covers, and the chapter note's exemption (registry plugins, crates a registry plugin chains to) does not apply. `disable` is checked only where `enabled_dependencies` seeds the worklist. The fixed-point loop in `plugins::active_plugins` (`pms.load_plugin` then `record_active`) has no `is_disabled` check. Neither does `record_active`, which pushes each chained edge as `CargoPm::id_for(&edge.name, None)`. Reproduced with the built binary. I copied `tests/fixtures/crate-path-multihop0` without `dot-symposium`, so the app depends on path crates crate-a, crate-b and crate-c, and crate-b's `[[package.metadata.symposium.plugins]] source.cargo = "crate-c"`. The config had `[defaults] symposium-recommendations = false, user-plugins = false` and `[plugins] auto-enable = ["*"], disable = ["crate-c"]`. `cargo-agents sync` printed "installed skill c-guidance for claude" and created `.claude/skills/c-guidance`. `cargo-agents status` reported "crate-c 0.1.0 — declined (`[plugins] disable`)". So the disabled crate-c was activated even though `auto-enable` and `disable` both name it, and `status` disagrees with what activation actually did. That contradicts the `decide` comment "Activation agrees (see `record_active`)".
requirement: Symposium MUST NOT activate a dependency plugin or `use`d crate that `[plugins] disable` names, even when `[plugins] auto-enable` or a `[plugins] use` entry also names it.
